script.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: It states that the house does not measure up in the people's eyes. God asks how it appears to them; the passage does not give their answer.
It applies God's assurance that He is with the people directly to the individual baker, although the passage addresses Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people of the land.
The statement that the people are building God's house needs a reference outside this passage, such as Haggai 1:14–15.
The oven comparison makes God's promise the subject of a joke.
The Jordan crossing and its timing relative to the departure from Egypt are facts outside this passage and need references.
Identifying David as Israel's king is a fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
The jokes about packing a bag and leaving the building make the Holy Spirit the subject of the humor.
The passage says God's Spirit remains among the people, not that the Spirit remains in the building.
The comparison 'small potatoes' mentions a food other than cookies.
Calling the question a trick comments on the lesson's own question.
It says the people looked at the house as though it were nothing. God asks whether it appears that way; their answer is not given.
The passage does not say the workers are busy. It says God tells the people to work.
The passage addresses Joshua but does not say he was present in an audience.
The delivery joke makes God's claim to the silver and gold the subject of the humor.
It states that the house looked like nothing. God asks whether it appears that way; the passage does not report the answer.
